metadata.title: Score-Based Generative Modeling through Stochastic Differential Equations (Song et al., 2020)
metadata.framework: continuous-time diffusion via SDEs unifying score matching and denoising diffusion
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of arXiv:2011.13456.

nodes.name: Forward SDE (diffusion process)
nodes.statement: A continuous-time diffusion process defined by the Ito SDE: $d\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, t) dt + g(t) d\mathbf{w}$ for $t \in [0, T]$, where $\mathbf{f}(\cdot, t): \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}^d$ is the drift, $g(\cdot): \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the scalar diffusion coefficient, and $\mathbf{w}$ is a standard Wiener process. The process transforms data $\mathbf{x}(0) \sim p_0$ into noise $\mathbf{x}(T) \sim p_T \approx \mathcal{N}(0, I)$.

nodes.name: Reverse-time SDE
nodes.statement: By Anderson (1982), the reverse of the forward SDE is also an SDE: $d\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, t) - g(t)^2 \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log p_t(\mathbf{x})] dt + g(t) d\bar{\mathbf{w}}$ where $\bar{\mathbf{w}}$ is a reverse-time Wiener process and $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log p_t(\mathbf{x})$ is the score function of the marginal density $p_t$ at time $t$.

nodes.name: Score function and time-dependent score network
nodes.statement: The score function $\nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log p_t(\mathbf{x})$ is the gradient of the log-density of the noisy data at time $t$. A neural network $\mathbf{s}_\theta(\mathbf{x}, t) \approx \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log p_t(\mathbf{x})$ is trained to approximate the score at all noise levels simultaneously.

nodes.name: Score matching training objective
nodes.statement: The score network is trained by minimizing the continuous-time denoising score matching objective: $\mathcal{J}(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_{t \sim \mathcal{U}[0,T]} \left[ \lambda(t) \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}(0)} \mathbb{E}_{\mathbf{x}(t)|\mathbf{x}(0)} \left[ \| \mathbf{s}_\theta(\mathbf{x}(t), t) - \nabla_{\mathbf{x}(t)} \log p_{0t}(\mathbf{x}(t) | \mathbf{x}(0)) \|^2 \right] \right]$ where $p_{0t}(\mathbf{x}(t)|\mathbf{x}(0))$ is the transition kernel (Gaussian for affine SDEs) and $\lambda(t)$ is a weighting function.

nodes.name: Variance Preserving SDE (VP-SDE) = DDPM
nodes.statement: The VP-SDE: $d\mathbf{x} = -\frac{1}{2} \beta(t) \mathbf{x} \, dt + \sqrt{\beta(t)} \, d\mathbf{w}$ where $\beta(t)$ is a continuous-time noise schedule. The VP-SDE is the continuous-time limit of the DDPM discrete forward process: taking $T \to \infty$ with the DDPM schedule $\beta_i$ recovers the VP-SDE via Euler-Maruyama discretization.

nodes.name: Variance Exploding SDE (VE-SDE) = SMLD
nodes.statement: The VE-SDE: $d\mathbf{x} = \sqrt{\frac{d[\sigma^2(t)]}{dt}} \, d\mathbf{w}$ (no drift). This is the continuous-time limit of the score matching with Langevin dynamics (SMLD) approach of Song & Ermon (2019), where noise levels $\sigma_1 < \cdots < \sigma_N$ define a sequence of increasingly noisy distributions.

nodes.name: Probability flow ODE
nodes.statement: For any SDE, there exists a deterministic ODE whose trajectories share the same marginal densities $p_t$: $d\mathbf{x} = \left[ \mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x}, t) - \frac{1}{2} g(t)^2 \nabla_{\mathbf{x}} \log p_t(\mathbf{x}) \right] dt$. This 'probability flow ODE' enables: (1) exact likelihood computation via the instantaneous change-of-variables formula; (2) deterministic sampling; (3) latent-space manipulation.

nodes.name: Predictor-corrector sampling
nodes.statement: Sampling combines a 'predictor' (numerical SDE solver step, e.g., Euler-Maruyama or ancestral sampling) with a 'corrector' (score-based MCMC step, e.g., Langevin dynamics). The predictor follows the reverse SDE; the corrector refines the sample at each noise level using the score estimate.

nodes.name: DDPM and SMLD are discretizations of SDEs
nodes.statement: The DDPM forward process $q(\mathbf{x}_t|\mathbf{x}_{t-1}) = \mathcal{N}(\sqrt{1-\beta_t} \mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \beta_t I)$ is the Euler-Maruyama discretization of the VP-SDE $d\mathbf{x} = -\frac{1}{2}\beta(t)\mathbf{x} \, dt + \sqrt{\beta(t)} \, d\mathbf{w}$. Similarly, SMLD's noise perturbation kernels are discretizations of the VE-SDE. This unifies both approaches as instances of a single continuous-time framework.
assumptions: DDPM forward process (cf. Ho et al. 2020)

nodes.name: Exact log-likelihood via probability flow ODE
nodes.statement: Using the probability flow ODE and the instantaneous change-of-variables formula (continuous normalizing flow): $\log p_0(\mathbf{x}(0)) = \log p_T(\mathbf{x}(T)) + \int_0^T \nabla \cdot \tilde{\mathbf{f}}_\theta(\mathbf{x}(t), t) \, dt$ where $\tilde{\mathbf{f}}_\theta = \mathbf{f} - \frac{1}{2} g^2 \mathbf{s}_\theta$. This enables exact (unbiased) log-likelihood evaluation, not just a bound.
conclusions: Exact log-likelihood computation (not a variational bound)
Score-based models can be evaluated as continuous normalizing flows

nodes.name: State-of-the-art generation and likelihood
nodes.statement: Score-based SDE models achieve FID 2.20 on CIFAR-10 (unconditional, VP-SDE with predictor-corrector sampling), surpassing DDPM's 3.17 and all prior diffusion and score-matching models. Additionally, the probability flow ODE achieves 2.99 bits/dim on CIFAR-10, competitive with the best autoregressive models.
assumptions: Score network trained with denoising score matching (DP_SDE.4)
conclusions: FID 2.20 on CIFAR-10 (new state of the art among likelihood-based models)
